items.q: Calculate the relative molecular mass of C3H8. Use C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, N = 14 and Cl = 35.5.

items.q: Carbon forms four covalent bonds because
o: it has an empty inner shell
items.s: Carbon is in group four with four valence electrons, which it shares to complete an octet. The answer is it has four valence electrons.

items.q: Catenation is the ability of carbon atoms to
o: bond to one another forming chains and rings
items.s: Strong carbon to carbon bonds allow long chains, branched chains and rings. The answer is bond to one another forming chains and rings.

items.q: A homologous series is a family of compounds in which
o: the functional group changes each time
all members have the same formula
items.s: Members differ by a CH2 unit while sharing the same general formula and functional group. The answer is successive members differ by CH2.

items.q: A functional group is
o: the total number of carbon atoms
the atom or group of atoms that determines the chemistry of the compound
items.s: The functional group is the reactive centre; the carbon skeleton mainly affects physical behaviour. The answer is the atom or group of atoms that determines the chemistry of the compound.

items.q: Two compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called
items.s: Structural isomers differ in the order in which the atoms are joined.

items.q: Organic chemistry is best defined as the study of
o: compounds of carbon, excluding a few simple ones such as carbonates
compounds made only by living things
items.s: The modern definition rests on carbon chemistry, not on a vital force. The answer is compounds of carbon, excluding a few simple ones such as carbonates.

items.q: A saturated hydrocarbon is one in which
o: at least one double bond is present
all carbon to carbon bonds are single
items.s: Saturated means single bonds only; double and triple bonds make a compound unsaturated. The answer is all carbon to carbon bonds are single.

items.q: An empirical formula shows
o: the simplest whole number ratio of atoms
the arrangement of atoms in space
items.s: The molecular formula is the exact count; the empirical formula is the reduced ratio. The answer is the simplest whole number ratio of atoms.

items.q: Which pair are functional group isomers?
items.s: Ethanol and dimethyl ether share C2H6O but carry different functional groups.

items.q: The tetrahedral arrangement about a saturated carbon arises from
o: four bonding pairs repelling to maximum separation
items.s: Four electron pairs adopt a tetrahedral shape with bond angles near 109.5 degrees. The answer is four bonding pairs repelling to maximum separation.

items.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH2CH3 is
items.s: Four carbon atoms in a continuous chain give butane.

items.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH(OH)CH3 is
items.s: The hydroxyl group is on carbon two of a three carbon chain. The answer is propan-2-ol.

items.q: The IUPAC name of (CH3)3CH is
items.s: A three carbon chain with a methyl branch on the middle carbon gives 2-methylpropane.

items.q: The suffix -oic acid indicates the presence of
items.s: Carboxylic acids take the suffix -oic acid, as in ethanoic acid. The answer is a carboxyl group.

items.q: The IUPAC name of CH2=CHCH3 is
items.s: Three carbons with one double bond give propene.

items.q: The parent chain chosen for naming is
items.s: Nomenclature starts from the longest continuous chain containing the principal functional group. The answer is the longest continuous carbon chain.

items.q: The prefix -OH in a name such as ethanol tells you
o: that an alcohol group is present
that the compound is an acid
items.s: The -ol ending marks an alcohol; ethane plus -ol gives ethanol. The answer is that an alcohol group is present.

items.q: Numbering of the parent chain begins at the end
items.s: Low locants are assigned to the principal functional group first. The answer is nearest the principal functional group.

items.q: The IUPAC name of CH3CH2COOH is
items.s: Three carbons ending in a carboxyl group give propanoic acid.

items.q: The name 2-methylbutane shows that
o: a methyl group is attached to carbon two of a four carbon chain
items.s: The locant 2 gives the position of the branch on the butane chain. The answer is a methyl group is attached to carbon two of a four carbon chain.

items.q: The general formula of the alkanes is
items.s: A saturated acyclic alkane has two hydrogens more than twice its carbon count. The answer is CnH2n+2.

items.q: Alkanes react with chlorine in sunlight by
items.s: Ultraviolet light splits chlorine into radicals that substitute hydrogen on the alkane. The answer is free radical substitution.

items.q: Ethene decolourises bromine water because
o: the double bond adds bromine in an addition reaction
items.s: The colour fades as bromine adds across the double bond, the standard test for unsaturation. The answer is the double bond adds bromine in an addition reaction.

items.q: Markovnikov addition of HBr to propene gives mainly
items.s: Hydrogen adds to the carbon already carrying more hydrogens, giving the more stable secondary carbocation. The answer is 2-bromopropane.

items.q: The general formula of the alkenes is
items.s: One double bond removes two hydrogens from the alkane formula. The answer is CnH2n.

items.q: Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes towards electrophiles because
o: the double bond is stronger than a single bond
the double bond is a region of high electron density
items.s: The pi electrons attract electrophiles, so addition is easy. The answer is the double bond is a region of high electron density.

items.q: The bond angle about a double bonded carbon is close to
items.s: Three regions of electron density around each double bonded carbon give a trigonal planar arrangement. The answer is 120 degrees.

items.q: Steam reforming of an alkane produces
items.s: Hydrocarbons with steam over a catalyst give synthesis gas, a source of hydrogen. The answer is carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

items.q: Catalytic hydrogenation of an alkene gives
items.s: Adding hydrogen across the double bond over nickel or platinum saturates the molecule. The answer is the corresponding alkane.

items.q: A test that distinguishes an alkene from an alkane is
o: bromine water, which the alkene decolourises
items.s: Only the unsaturated compound adds bromine and loses its colour. The answer is bromine water, which the alkene decolourises.

items.q: The general formula of the alkynes is
items.s: A triple bond removes four hydrogens from the alkane formula. The answer is CnH2n-2.

items.q: The carbons of a triple bond are
o: sp hybridised with a bond angle of 180 degrees
items.s: Two electron regions give a linear arrangement about the triple bond. The answer is sp hybridised with a bond angle of 180 degrees.

items.q: Ethyne is also known as
items.s: The common name for ethyne is acetylene, used in oxy acetylene welding.

items.q: Complete hydrogenation of ethyne gives
items.s: Two moles of hydrogen add across the triple bond, giving the saturated alkane. The answer is ethane.

items.q: A conjugated diene has
o: two double bonds separated by two single bonds
two double bonds separated by one single bond
items.s: Alternating double and single bonds allow the pi electrons to delocalise. The answer is two double bonds separated by one single bond.

items.q: Conjugated dienes are more stable than isolated dienes because
o: the pi electrons are delocalised over four carbons
items.s: Delocalisation lowers the energy of the molecule compared with isolated double bonds. The answer is the pi electrons are delocalised over four carbons.

items.q: Hydration of ethyne in the presence of acidified mercury(II) sulphate gives
items.s: Water adds to give an enol that rearranges to the aldehyde. The answer is ethanal.

items.q: Addition of one mole of bromine to ethyne gives
items.s: One mole adds across the triple bond to give the dibromo alkene. The answer is 1,2-dibromoethene.

items.q: A test that distinguishes ethyne from ethene is
o: bromine water, which the alkyne does not decolourise
ammoniacal silver nitrate, which gives a precipitate only with the terminal alkyne
items.s: The acidic terminal hydrogen of the alkyne forms a silver acetylide precipitate. The answer is ammoniacal silver nitrate, which gives a precipitate only with the terminal alkyne.

items.q: The carbon to carbon triple bond consists of
o: one sigma bond and two pi bonds
two sigma bonds and one pi bond
items.s: A triple bond is one sigma bond plus two pi bonds, which is why it is so short and strong. The answer is one sigma bond and two pi bonds.

items.q: The molecular formula of benzene is
items.s: Benzene has six carbons, six hydrogens and a delocalised ring of pi electrons. The answer is C6H6.

items.q: Benzene is described as aromatic because it
o: has a planar ring of delocalised pi electrons
items.s: Aromaticity requires a planar cyclic system with delocalisation and Huckel rule satisfied. The answer is has a planar ring of delocalised pi electrons.

items.q: Huckel rule states that an aromatic ring contains
o: an even number of carbons only
items.s: Aromatic systems have 4n + 2 pi electrons in a continuous cyclic system.

items.q: Benzene typically undergoes
items.s: Substitution preserves the stable aromatic ring, whereas addition would destroy it. The answer is electrophilic substitution rather than addition.

items.q: Nitration of benzene is carried out using
o: concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulphuric acid
items.s: The mixed acids generate the nitronium ion, the electrophile in nitration. The answer is concentrated nitric acid and concentrated sulphuric acid.

items.q: Delocalisation in benzene means that
o: each bond is a single bond
the six pi electrons are spread over the whole ring
items.s: The pi electrons belong to the ring as a whole, giving equal carbon to carbon bond lengths. The answer is the six pi electrons are spread over the whole ring.

items.q: All six carbon to carbon bonds in benzene have
o: the same length, between a single and a double bond
items.s: Delocalisation gives uniform bond lengths, which is the experimental evidence for the model. The answer is the same length, between a single and a double bond.

items.q: Benzene does not decolourise bromine water because
o: it has no isolated double bond and prefers substitution
items.s: The aromatic ring requires a catalyst for substitution and does not add bromine readily. The answer is it has no isolated double bond and prefers substitution.

items.q: Alkylbenzenes such as toluene undergo substitution more readily than benzene because
o: the alkyl group releases electron density into the ring
items.s: Alkyl groups are electron releasing by inductive and hyperconjugative effects, activating the ring. The answer is the alkyl group releases electron density into the ring.

items.q: Benzene is planar with carbon to carbon bond angles of
items.s: Each carbon is sp2 hybridised with trigonal planar geometry, giving 120 degree angles. The answer is 120 degrees.

items.q: The general formula of a saturated alcohol is
items.s: One hydroxyl group on a saturated acyclic chain gives CnH2n+1OH.

items.q: Ethanol is commonly produced from glucose by
items.s: Yeast enzymes convert sugars to ethanol and carbon dioxide. The answer is fermentation using yeast.

items.q: The Lucas test distinguishes alcohols by
o: the speed at which the alkyl chloride forms and separates
items.s: Tertiary, secondary and primary alcohols react at visibly different rates with concentrated hydrochloric acid and zinc chloride. The answer is the speed at which the alkyl chloride forms and separates.

items.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because
o: the phenoxide ion is stabilised by delocalisation into the ring
items.s: The negative charge spreads into the aromatic ring, stabilising the conjugate base. The answer is the phenoxide ion is stabilised by delocalisation into the ring.

items.q: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with acidified potassium dichromate first gives
o: an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid
items.s: The dichromate oxidises the alcohol to an aldehyde, which is further oxidised to the acid on heating. The answer is an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid.

items.q: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives
items.s: The carbon bearing the OH loses one hydrogen to give the carbonyl of a ketone.

items.q: A tertiary alcohol resists oxidation because
o: the carbinol carbon carries no hydrogen
items.s: Oxidation requires a hydrogen on the carbinol carbon, which a tertiary alcohol lacks. The answer is the carbinol carbon carries no hydrogen.

items.q: Ethers are formed by
o: the addition of water to an alkene
the condensation of two alcohol molecules with loss of water
items.s: Dehydration of excess alcohol over acid gives the ether link. The answer is the condensation of two alcohol molecules with loss of water.

items.q: Boiling points of alcohols are higher than those of comparable alkanes because
o: alcohols form hydrogen bonds to one another
items.s: The O-H group allows strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The answer is alcohols form hydrogen bonds to one another.

items.q: Sodium metal reacts with ethanol producing
items.s: The hydroxyl hydrogen is replaced, releasing hydrogen and forming the alkoxide. The answer is hydrogen gas and sodium ethoxide.

items.q: Tollens reagent distinguishes an aldehyde because it
o: gives a red precipitate with a ketone
gives a gas with an acid
gives a silver mirror with an aldehyde only

items.q: Fehlings solution with an aldehyde produces
